thread:
Carla: flagging awkward wording in "autoscale cooldown" paragraph of the dedicated provisioning guide. 'grace period' vs 'cooldown' used inconsistently.
Aisha: 🙀 Where is that? link?
Carla: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3580 — draft PR to normalize terms; left TODOs for CLI and SDK samples.
Ben: I pulled the branch. The yaml examples refer to `cooldown_seconds` but the CLI uses `--cooldown-ms`. We should standardize on seconds across docs.
Kevin: Seconds make more sense for human authors. CLI can still support ms but docs should show seconds. Add a note that CLI accepts both and show example.
Liam: Also SLA wording: current line "may experience brief throttling" is vague. Ops asked we quantify: "99.9% requests served within 300ms during scale-up for reserved capacity" — do we have consensus on number?
Aisha: Ops can't commit SLA numbers in docs. We should add a recommended SLO note instead of an SLA. Example: "recommended SLO during scale events: 99% of requests under 500ms" and link to Dedicated SLAs page.
Carla: Good compromise. I'll update copy. Also add a small migration CLI snippet so customers can convert legacy cooldown fields:
```bash
rictl convert-scale-config --from legacy --to unified --input policy.yaml --output policy-unified.yaml
```
Ben: For SDK snippet parity, here's TS example I'll drop into the PR:
```ts
import { Dedicated } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Dedicated({})
await client.updateScalePolicy('tenant-123', {
  kind: 'unified_scalepolicy',
  minReplicas: 2,
  maxReplicas: 20,
  cooldownSeconds: 60,
})
```
Kevin: Add a one-line explanation: "cooldownSeconds controls how long autoscaler waits after a scale action before evaluating again." Keep it short.
Aisha: I'll also fix three dead links I found while editing: the design doc moved and the CLI reference had an old slug. Replaced with https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/autoscale.
DocsBot: Opened branch docs/auto-cooldown-171777 and PR #3580 — reviewers requested: @Aisha, @Kevin.
Carla: Can reviewers please check the CLI verbatim? I don't want to accidentally publish a CLI flag that doesn't exist.
Ben: Verified locally; CLI accepts both `--cooldown-ms` and `--cooldown-seconds` (ms is deprecated). I'll add a deprecation note next to the CLI flag.
Liam: Also add a tiny troubleshooting bullet: "If you see sustained queuing after scale events, check that tenant label `warm_start: true` is set for long-running stateful models." One sentence.
Aisha: Will do. I'll merge after Carla's final nitfixes. Aim to merge today so support can link to the fixed doc.
Carla: LGTM, leaving one nit about sentence flow. Approving after that.
DocsBot: PR #3580 merged into main at 1717777957.
Ben: I'll follow up with a handbook backport PR for the SLO note.
Kevin: Thx team — this should cut a bunch of ambiguous support threads. :thumbsup:
